results.quote: Its applicant figures were internally inconsistent: over 200 applicants with about half admitted in one place, 225 with about 45% admitted in another.
results.finding: The inconsistency is stated but never tied to what it shows (that the alliance's own figures need their definitions attached and cannot be taken at face value); both flow readers read it as a digression.

All other evidence is introduced and read: the promise table and Figure 1, the commercetools table and its three readings, the two INFERENCE callouts, the pricing and Nexus facts, the principles table and Figure 2, the survey figures, the cost and fit tables with Figure 3, and the closing scenario evidence.

results.draft_locus: Adobe, the Forks and Commerce.com: Composable as a Deployment Option ¶1
results.quote: Adobe, the community forks of its open-source edition, and Commerce.com show the word being absorbed rather than adopted.
results.finding: Declared similarity carrying over Shopware absorbing integration and payments; the opening sentence makes no link back to Shopware, so the likeness between the cases is not expressed.

results.quote: 1. When a vendor or agency says "composable", which of the four 2020 words do they mean, and which of the alliance's three 2026 principles?
results.finding: Declared a cause_effect sentence carrying over the take-aways; the list starts with no lead-in, so nothing says the questions follow from the take-aways.

All other paragraph and section transitions express their declared relationship at the boundary (e.g. 'is another matter' contrast, 'Three things stand out. First' sequence, 'The second clue' sequence, 'point the same way' similarity, 'can therefore be tested' cause_effect).

results.quote: Who must connect and run those pieces? This chapter's claim gives the answer.
results.finding: The opening restates the thesis near verbatim after KEY POINTS and the failure patterns, and Introduction ¶6 repeats the source list from ¶3; the reader meets the claim (and the 37%) several times before the first section. The spec requires the claim and roadmap, not the repeated wording.
results.corroborated_by: flowB_reader: point 1 (the opening is crowded; the claim repeats the KEY POINTS almost word for word)

results.quote: **Where we are in the order's journey.** Eva buys a jacket from Kestrel & Pine, the fictional outdoor brand.
results.finding: flowA: the run-in paragraph 'sits between the alliance history and the claim' and breaks the move; the spec's order (pieces, then who connects them, then the claim) is sound, but the run-in label makes it read as an aside instead of the example that sets up p05's question.
results.corroborated_by: flowB_reader: reordering 3 (fold the 'Where we are in the order's journey' paragraph into the claim paragraph)

results.quote: Its applicant figures were internally inconsistent: over 200 applicants with about half admitted in one place, 225 with about 45% admitted in another.
results.finding: flowA: 'a side detail that does nothing for the argument at that point. I re-read it to check whether it mattered.' The spec wants it as evidence that the alliance's figures need definitions attached; the prose does not say so.
results.corroborated_by: flowB_reader: point 3 (a digression that the argument never uses)

results.quote: Either the business grew about 10% in three months or the units differ; the releases do not say which, and neither should you.
results.finding: flowA: '"Neither should you" is puzzling: neither should you say which?' The phrase obscures the intended advice (do not guess which).
results.corroborated_by: flowB_reader: point 5 (had to re-read 'neither should you')

results.quote: Saleor Cloud, an API-only platform
results.finding: flowA: '"34 integrations at Kestrel & Pine" and Saleor Cloud appear without introduction. Saleor is mentioned nowhere else.' The table row needs a word on why Saleor's pricing is the example.
results.corroborated_by: flowB_reader: point 8 (the Licenses row brings in Saleor Cloud out of nowhere)

results.quote: Kestrel & Pine ([[meet-kestrel-and-pine]]), in the book's scenario, received such a proposal in February 2027
results.finding: flowA: the proposal first appears inside the cost section and the decision comes two sections later; flowB: the opener 'The storefront line deserves a worked illustration' announces less than the paragraph covers and the 2027 date jars. The spec splits the proposal (costs) and the decline (kp, 'costed above'); the prose does not frame the proposal as the case the kp section returns to, nor point back to it there.
results.corroborated_by: flowB_reader: point 9 ('received such a proposal in February 2027' made me stop; scope wider than announced)

results.draft_locus: What Kestrel & Pine Takes From It ¶1 (Figure 4)
results.quote: The 2020 promise asked the merchant to build the storefront...
results.finding: flowA: Figure 4 'is about the promise against the 2026 products, so it is out of place there.' The spec places it here to show Waypoint's shape as the one the vendors' 2026 products attach to; the caption does not name Waypoint, so the link is lost.
results.corroborated_by: flowB_reader: point 10 (Figure 4 reads as out of place in the Kestrel & Pine section)

Opens on a puzzling scenario (one service, shared identifiers), bridges from chapters 47-48, states the claim and gives a roadmap.
No bare summary or new material; the conclusion answers the hook, separates established from context-dependent findings and ends in questions and closings.
What to Take Away ¶1 answers the question from the record; the questions and the Part XI test state what the reader does with it.
'The merchant at the start of this chapter wanted to replace its search service without replacing checkout and the catalog' answers the hook directly.

Reader names the storefront, join owner/version/renewal, reference-customer and kept-platform questions, more joins all the brand's, the 37%, commercetools' modules, Group-stage fit and one owned service beside a kept platform.

Reader treats both figures as the alliance's own claims, notes ROI undefined, the inconsistent applicant totals, keeps unit/date/definition attached, names the 37% against interest and the missing independent study (omits the commercetools and Shopware examples, not the substance).
Reader answers no: different axes, open core but hub-shaped, GMV pricing, Nexus and Payments, commercetools proprietary and service-shaped, choose on upgrades and joins.
Intro reader predicts the section order, the dated public-record evidence with labeled limits, Eva's order and the tone; it does not mention the failure-pattern names, a minor gap.
